governanceNotes: D1 batch 52 (2026-09-24): deferred. Class/umbrella and duplicate-scope screens recorded 2026-09-24: the catalog identity is named "Leukemia (Acute & Chronic)", which aggregates acute lymphoblastic, acute myeloid, chronic lymphocytic, chronic myeloid, and other phenotypes, and the catalog already carries member identities that own the secondary-condition pathways - chronic-b-cell-leukemias already authors an anemia window and hairy-cell-leukemia already authors an anemia window, while leukemia itself is the <target> of four secondary-leukemia windows (myelodysplastic-syndrome, essential-thrombocythemia, polycythemia-vera, and primary-myelofibrosis). Authoring a generic leukemia-to-anemia or leukemia-to-thrombocytopenia window would therefore restate the member identities' own pathways under the umbrella label, the same class-scope disposition the program applied to gastrointestinal-cancers and head-and-neck-cancers, where the organ-site member identities own the pathways.

Evidence and prior-closure screens recorded 2026-09-24: the harvested leukemia-to-breast-cancer proposition remains FINAL-CLOSED under FINAL-CLOSE-PROPOSITION-MISMATCH (PMID 40445187) and is not reasserted. Within the identity's own evidence base the located quantitative outcomes are treatment-context and treatment-mediated rather than leukemia-attributable: cytopenia and infection outcomes are reported during and after intensive induction or salvage chemotherapy (for example a randomized induction trial reporting grade 3 or higher infections in 32% versus 67% and severe thrombocytopenia duration of 13 versus 19 days by regimen, PMID 40009498), bleeding outcomes are reported in thrombocytopenic acute leukemic patients with venous thromboembolism (PMID 35845011), and the largest located pediatric cohort outcome was post-treatment ocular morbidity in which cataract development was associated with cranial radiation (PMID 35187841) - i.e., post-chemotherapy and post-radiation complications, which under the program's treatment-mediation guard belong to the treatment rather than to the disease identity. Reopening condition: a governance scope decision on the umbrella, or an umbrella-specific cohort quantifying a catalog-fit secondary with phenotype, treatment, and chronology adjustment.
